raw_response:
I farm 8 mu, and at my age I do not chase fancy changes. I start from what has held yield here in Quzhou County and then adjust a little by crop price, labor, and water. Since I have well irrigation, I will keep the main land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is still the steadiest way for me to get grain. I will put 6 mu into wheat followed by summer maize on the same 6 mu, and I will keep 2 mu in cotton so I still have some cash crop income. With my education and years in the field, I do not only copy habit; I look at soil fertility, target yield, and how much money I can put into fertilizer without squeezing pesticide and irrigation. For wheat, I will feed it a bit heavier because a weak wheat stand is hard to fix later, and I have water so fertilizer can work. For maize after wheat, I will keep nitrogen strong but not waste too much phosphate because the wheat season already leaves some base fertility behind. For cotton, I will not plant too much area because it takes more management, but on 2 mu I can still watch it closely and keep the field clean. I would rather spend a little more on fertilizer than lose yield, but I will still keep rates within what I know works on fields like mine around here.
